newsitem.title: UK: Unions plan UPS day of action on May 22.
newsitem.headline: Unions plan UPS day of action on May 22.

text.p: Unions representing United Parcel Service of America are planning an international day of action on May 22 against the U.S. express company, a spokeman for the London-based International Transport Workers Federation (ITF) said.

The day of action will focus on the creation and maintenance of full-time work within the company and an end to contracting out of drivers' work, ITF communications secretary Richard Flint told Reuters.
He added it will also support the 900 UPS Italian staff who were told on March 6 that the company was cutting 150 jobs in the country.

"And it is intended to demonstrate that UPS unions want to work together in this area and hopefully encourage the company to talk to the UPS-ITF World Trade Union Council (set up in mid-February)," Flint said.
"The U.S. Teamsters have committed themselves to supporting the day of action," he added, and are offering substantial help in its organisation.
"Each union will decide on how best to organise its own action," Flint said. He gave no details of what form the protests might take.
A UPS spokeswoman said she was unable to comment on the unions' plans for May 22.

UPS unions in Italy, Spain, France and Belgium have said they are very keen on the proposed action and contacts are now underway with unions representing UPS workers elsewhere in Europe, including Britain.
The ITF is also talking to member unions in Canada, Japan, Taiwan and Brazil, Flint added.
Meanwhile, industry sources noted that the Teamsters current four-year UPS-Teamster contract in the U.S., where the union says it represents nearly 200,000 workers, is up for renewal this July.
Teamster president, Ron Carey wrote to UPS in March expressing the union's "strong possible protest over the treatment of the company's workers in Italy."
Under Italian labour law, UPS would have been able to begin laying off the 150 workers within 45 days from March 6.
Since then there have been a series of meetings between management, unions as well as government officials.
And earlier this week, UPS Italia issued a statement saying "there is space for an agreement" between the two sides and the date for the earliest staff layoffs has now been put back to May 30.
